messages:
mona: Auditor Lee just asked for a tight SOC2 evidence bundle focused on the privsep RBAC change that touched KMS access. They want replayable artifacts + a short playback. Can someone own?

karim: I can own the runbook and manifest. We should include PR + approver, change ticket, sanitized CloudTrail snippets for kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey, KMS key policy, rotation history export, SIEM trace, and a rollback demo with exact commands and redacted outputs.

auditor_lee: Ideal bundle: 1) infra PR (link + who approved + timestamp), 2) change approval ticket, 3) sanitized events showing service principal invoking kms:Decrypt/GenerateDataKey on the CMK, 4) key rotation CSV or screenshot + CMK ARN, 5) SIEM correlation demonstrating alert -> principal -> key ARN, 6) brief description of how privileged separation (privsep) prevents cross-tenant decrypts and how ephemeral DEKs are handled. Prefer artifacts that can be replayed locally (sanitized).

tara: Draft Splunk query to extract events (will redact before upload):
```splunk
index=cloudtrail sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail eventName IN ("Decrypt","GenerateDataKey") requestParameters.keyId="arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:555555555555:key/privsep-01"
| table _time userIdentity.principalId userIdentity.type eventName requestParameters.keyId requestParameters.ciphertextBlob errorMessage
| sort _time
```

karim: Sanitization snippet (jq) to minimize fields and remove account ids:
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=kms.amazonaws.com --start-time 2024-11-10T00:00:00Z --end-time 2024-11-10T23:59:59Z --query 'Events[].CloudTrailEvent' > raw_cloudtrail.json
jq 'map({t:.eventTime, actor:.userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName // .userIdentity.principalId, type:.userIdentity.type, event:.eventName, key:.requestParameters.keyId})' raw_cloudtrail.json > artifacts/sanitized-kms-privsep.json
```

mona: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/612 (changed binding: infra-privsep -> kms-decrypt). Approval ticket: JIRA INF-7622, approved by @karim at 2024-11-10T09:41:00Z. I'll snapshot the PR diff and redact resource-specific ids.

auditor_lee: For rotation proof a CSV export is fine. Please include the CMK ARN and list principals with rotation permission. Also include any KMS key policy edits that were part of the change.

tara: We'll include a small envelope-encryption diagram (KEK/DEK) and note that DEKs are ephemeral and not persisted beyond 2 minutes in the serving tier (cache TTL: 120s).

karim: SIEM rule ID: SIEM-2024-6420. I'll pull the correlation showing alert id, correlated ticket, matched events and principal. We'll produce a replay file that maps alert -> event indices in the sanitized-kms JSON.

evidence-bot: Upload guidance: use secure bucket s3://redwood-audit-evidence/INF-7622/2024-11-10. Use presigned URLs (24h TTL) and include manifest.txt with filenames, SHA256 checksums, and control mapping. Label files per manifest.

tara: For rollback demo auditor asked for proof that after revert the service principal's Decrypt fails. We'll capture shell outputs (redact account ids) as both screenshots and plaintext. Example test commands we will run and capture: 
```bash
# create sample ciphertext using CMK
aws kms generate-data-key --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:555555555555:key/privsep-01 --key-spec AES_256 --query CiphertextBlob --output text | base64 --decode > sample.ct
# before revert (expect success)
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://sample.ct --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:555555555555:key/privsep-01 --profile infra-privsep
# after revert (expect AccessDenied)
# revert RBAC binding and retry
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://sample.ct --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:555555555555:key/privsep-01 --profile infra-privsep
```

karim: We'll also include a short forensic hash chain: manifest entries with SHA256 for each artifact, and a signed manifest.txt (GPG-signed by approver) showing mapping: CONTROL-ID -> filename -> proof statement.

auditor_lee: Nice. Also include a short note on STS scoping: explain how AssumeRole and session policies prevent decryption across tenants. A one-paragraph description is enough.

mona: Owners: karim (runbook + manifest + PR snapshot), tara (sanitized logs + Splunk + replay script), mona (bundle assembly + upload). ETA: draft bundle by Thursday EOD. I'll post presigned link here when uploaded. :thumbsup:
